content:
Alex: Heads-up: finance flagged divergence between reported token spend and the billing ledger for last month. breakdown shows most variance coming from post-ingest enrichment path.
Priya: yup, we9re seeing duplicate token attributions when enrichers emit derivatives and the pipeline retries.
Ning: curious if this is instrumentation (counting before dedupe) or a semantic problem (we9re counting deltas incorrectly).
Alex: both, but short story: we increment a tenant9s token counter whenever an enriched envelope is processed, and we don9t have a canonical "final" record for an envelope. retries + parallel enrichers lead to double counts.
Jules: framing two options: (A) ledger-first model: maintain a single authoritative billing write at ingress/root; enrichers only attach delta metadata. (B) merge-on-read: allow multiple billing writes but merge them in post-processing by taking max(delta) per envelope or using a last-write wins watermark.
Priya: ledger-first simplifies accounting but loses per-enricher token detail unless we plumb deltas back synchronously. that adds latency on the hot path.
Ning: merge-on-read is eventually consistent and easier for throughput but complicates the billing pipeline and inflates storage for intermediate writes. also we need stable enrichment identifiers to merge correctly.
Alex: tradeoffs also include storage/compute costs. merge-on-read requires keeping enrichment events for the window; ledger-first centralizes work but forces a cross-service RPC or a small append-only ledger which we must scale.
Jules: another axis: accuracy vs cost. For high-volume tenants, we could switch to "estimated billing" using sampled token counts and a deterministic estimator; for low-volume tenants use exact accounting.
Priya: we can't provide estimates for enterprise customers with SLAs — they need exactness. but for self-serve tenants approximate billing is acceptable.
Ning: implementation idea hybrid: ingest writes a provisional billing record with envelope_id + baseline_tokens. enrichers asynchronously submit enrichment_delta and enrichment_hash. Billing reconciler merges deltas per envelope using max(delta) and a finalized flag. once reconciled, provisional record gets promoted to final.
Alex: that avoids synchronous calls but requires a reconciliation job and short-term state store. need to pick a retention window for reconciliation (e.g., 60s).
Jules: reconciliation window tradeoff: longer window reduces double-count risk but increases memory footprint for the reconciliation store and delays finalization. shorter window reduces memory but may miss late enrichers.
Priya: propose default window = 45s with per-tenant overrides. for Dedicated/enterprise tenants we can set longer windows or use ledger-first.
Ning: schema change: add fields on enrichment payload: enrichment_hash (string), delta_tokens (int), finalized (bool), enricher_version (string). billing record schema: envelope_id, baseline_tokens, reconciled_deltas[], finalized_at_ts.
Alex: important: enrichment_hash must be deterministic for same logical output. document hashing rules (stable JSON canonicalization + stable sort for tag arrays). otherwise merge fails.
Jules: also need tombstones when we detect misreported deltas (negative delta should be rejected). validation rules in reconciler.
Priya: metrics to track: reconciler_lag_p50/p99, double_count_rate (billing increments that were later rolled back), reconciliation_memory_bytes, reconciliation_hits/misses, per-tenant_reconcile_rate.
Ning: alerts: if double_count_rate > 1.3x baseline or reconciler_lag_p99 > 2x expectation, paging to eng-platform.
Alex: migration strategy:
- phase 0: proto schema + reconciler canary on 5% of tenants (non-enterprise) for 2 weeks.
- phase 1: enable finalized flag support and reconcilers for 30% tenants; surface metrics to finance.
- phase 2: for enterprise pods, offer ledger-first opt-in with synchronous delta writes behind feature flag.
- phase 3: GA and cleanup of provisional records after 30 days.
Jules: ops concerns: reconciliation store must be bounded per-tenant. propose max_entries_per_tenant=10000 and TTL=45s. LRU eviction policy + emit eviction metrics.
Priya: security/compliance: keep reconciliation data ephemeral; mark non-PII. encrypt at rest for Dedicated customers per KMS policy.
Ning: backward compatibility: enrichers that don9t implement the schema will default to delta_tokens=0 and finalized=true; reconciliation will treat them as no-op. we should inventory enrichers and prioritize updates.
Alex: action items:
- draft mini-RFC for hybrid reconciliation model and schema (Jules) :todo:
- implement reconciliation store prototype with LRU+TTL and Prom metrics (Ning) :in_progress:
- add enrichment schema contract + canonicalization guide and test vectors (Priya) :todo:
- finance dashboard: expose before/after reconciliation spend and double_count_reduction (Alex) :todo:
- create feature flags: recon-inline (ledger-first opt-in) and recon-canary (reconciler rollout) (InfraBot) :done
ObservabilityBot: feature_flag: recon-canary toggled for 5% of development tenants.
Alex: timeline: prototype this sprint, canary next week, expand after two measurement runs.
Priya: will add tests to the enrichment harness to validate deterministic hashing and delta semantics.
Jules: I'll owner the RFC and list of enrichers that need changes.
Ning: will start the reconciliation prototype and post perf numbers.
Alex: thanks all. goal: eliminate >90% of double-count cases and keep finalization latency below 2s p99 for non-enterprise tenants.
Priya: noted, thanks.
